claims.text: What the strip looks like Deep symmetric T-wave inversion or biphasic T waves in V2–V3, typically in a pain-free patient.
claims.quote: Wellens Syndrome: Deep symmetric T-wave inversions (Type B) or biphasic T waves (Type A) in V2–V3, typically in a pain-free patient.

claims.text: Aspects (abnormal in red) T waves: type A biphasic, up then down (25%); type B deeply and symmetrically inverted (75%)
claims.quote: Type A – Biphasic, with initial positivity and terminal negativity (25% of cases) Type B – Deeply and symmetrically inverted (75% of cases)

claims.text: Rhinehart criteria: in V2–V3 (may extend to V1–V6); pain-free; ST isoelectric or minimally raised (< 1 mm); no precordial Q waves; preserved R-wave progression; recent angina; normal or slightly raised markers
claims.quote: Rhinehart et al (2002) describe the following diagnostic criteria for Wellens syndrome: Deeply inverted or biphasic T waves in V2-3 (may extend to V1-6) ECG pattern present in pain-free state Isoelectric or minimally-elevated ST segment (< 1mm) No precordial Q waves Preserved precordial R wave progression Recent history of angina Normal or slightly elevated serum cardiac markers

claims.text: Usually seen pain-free; during pain the T waves may pseudonormalize — a reason every chest-pain patient needs serial ECGs
claims.quote: The pattern is usually present in the pain free state — it may be obscured during episodes of ischaemic chest pain, when there is “pseudonormalisation” of T waves in V2-3 Wellens syndrome is a key example of why all patients presenting with chest pain must have serial ECGs

claims.text: Causes (mechanism and diagnoses) Highly specific for critical LAD stenosis
claims.quote: It is highly specific for critical stenosis of the left anterior descending artery (LAD)

claims.text: Mechanism: after the LAD reperfuses (e.g., clot lysis, prehospital aspirin), pain resolves, ST elevation improves and the T waves become biphasic or inverted
claims.quote: Re-perfusion of the LAD (e.g. due to spontaneous clot lysis or prehospital aspirin) leads to resolution of chest pain. ST elevation improves and T waves become biphasic or inverted.

claims.text: Can follow vasospasm in normal arteries (e.g., cocaine), but it is safer to assume critical LAD stenosis and work up for angiography
claims.quote: Wellens syndrome may also occur in normal coronary arteries following an episode of vasospasm, as in this case of cocaine-induced vasospasm. However, it is safer to assume the worst (i.e. critical LAD stenosis) and work the patient up for an angiogram.

claims.text: Symptoms May be pain-free with normal or minimally raised enzymes — yet at extremely high risk of extensive anterior MI within days to weeks
claims.quote: Patients may be pain free by the time the ECG is taken, and have normal or minimally elevated cardiac enzymes. However, they are at extremely high risk for extensive anterior wall MI within the subsequent days to weeks

claims.text: Treatment Needs cath, not stress testing
Usually need invasive therapy; do poorly with medical management; may have MI or cardiac arrest if inappropriately stress tested
claims.quote: Due to the critical LAD stenosis, these patients usually require invasive therapy, do poorly with medical management, and may suffer MI or cardiac arrest if inappropriately stress tested
